email.body1:
Danielle, saw Daxko picked up Exercise.com and Vision late last year, pushing into boutique fitness and Boys & Girls Clubs nationwide.

That much new whitespace usually means more in-market accounts than business development can reach before they cool, and that is where pipeline leaks. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Daxko off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Danielle, quick follow-up for Daxko.

After acquisitions, the new-segment quota usually lands faster than headcount can. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to book to cover it, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Daxko needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Danielle, last bit of proof for Daxko.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Daxko's reply rate likely compares to other fitness-tech players. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Danielle, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating two acquisitions is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Daxko either way.
